cross_namespace_observations.question: whether 0 should render the singular ('0 जागृति') or an explicit =0 plural ('0 जागृतियाँ')
cross_namespace_observations.disposition_as_implementer: kept the singular on CLDR and core grounds; this audit's round-1 MAJOR was recorded as an open decision
cross_namespace_observations.this_round_position: ACCEPTED, and this audit's round-1 MAJOR is withdrawn
reasons: The binding hi style guide says, under Plurals: 'Categories: one / other — and one covers 0 and 1: "0 फ़ाइल" is singular.' The guide states it is binding for translators and the auditor.
The core glossary's plurals row records hi as 'one/other (0 is one)'.
Intl.PluralRules('hi').select(0) is 'one' (executed this round), so the shipped one/other message renders '0 जागृति' by CLDR, not by translator choice.

Core's committed Hindi carries the same one/other arms for the same noun (e.g. tui.schedule.fired '{count, plural, one {# जागृति} other {# जागृतियाँ}}'), so an =0 arm in the mobile catalogue alone would diverge from every core consumer of the same noun.
An =0 arm would also break arm parity with the English source, which the audit harness and the programme's mechanical contract both assume; that is a supporting reason, not the deciding one.

My round-1 claim that 'Hindi reads the plural after zero' contradicts the guide's explicit example. The guide wins; the finding was wrong on the evidence, and it is withdrawn rather than merely deferred.
